actions.action: Commit the update and event receipt together.
actions.mechanism: A unique event-ID receipt and business update share one transaction; acknowledgement follows successful commit.
actions.implementation: Insert the partner-scoped ID using a unique key. Only the successful inserter may update state. Roll back both on failure; acknowledge committed duplicates.
actions.check: Race concurrent deliveries of one ID. Assert one committed receipt and at most one business update.
actions.risk: External side effects cannot be protected by this database transaction alone.

actions.action: Gate entity updates on their revision.
actions.mechanism: An atomic revision comparison prevents older or equal revisions from changing already newer entity state.
actions.implementation: Within the receipt transaction, lock the entity and apply only an eligible higher revision. Record stale deliveries without updating. Retain revision markers across deletion.
actions.check: Deliver revisions 12, 10, 12 concurrently. Assert final revision 12 and no regression or repeated revision-12 update.
actions.risk: Incremental events require gap handling rather than blindly skipping missing revisions.

actions.action: Expire receipts only after the replay boundary.
actions.mechanism: A fixed first-seen deadline covers seven-day redelivery; processing grace protects deliveries admitted near expiry.
actions.implementation: Set expiry to first_seen plus seven days plus an enforced maximum processing delay. Never refresh on duplicates. Delete only after expiry; serialize cleanup with receipt access.
actions.check: Replay just before, exactly at, and just after seven days. Delay a boundary delivery through the processing limit; verify no repeated update.
actions.risk: Without a bounded processing delay, finite time-based retention alone cannot protect arbitrarily delayed requests.

actions.action: Budget physical receipt storage before deployment.
actions.mechanism: Compact receipts and measured database overhead keep deduplication storage below 2 GB without premature eviction.
actions.implementation: Store only scoped IDs and necessary timestamps; minimize indexes. Measure table, indexes, deletion overhead, and revision markers. Include grace-period population and cleanup backlog in capacity limits.
actions.check: Load the maximum retained population using representative ID lengths. Run cleanup under traffic; require peak durable deduplication storage below 2 GB.
actions.risk: Average ID length alone does not bound index, allocator, or operational overhead.

actions.action: Automate crash and replay fault injection.
actions.mechanism: Failures around transaction commit and acknowledgement expose update-without-receipt and replay races.
actions.implementation: Crash before commit, after commit before acknowledgement, and during acknowledgement. Replay each event, including concurrent duplicates, reordered revisions, and receipts undergoing expiry cleanup.
actions.check: Assert uncommitted work rolls back; committed updates never repeat; revisions never decrease; boundary behavior matches retention policy.
actions.risk: Tests must inspect business state, not merely successful HTTP responses.
